rooms.3516: The forest floor sags here into a broad sinkhole, a sunken bowl of black mud where rainwater stands in brown pools between the roots. Your boots sink to the ankle with every step, and each one comes free with a wet, sucking squelch. Gnarled oaks lean over the rim, their bared roots hanging like old rope above the water. Trails climb out of the hollow north to the crossroads, east toward the mountains, south onto a darker path, and west where the trees grow thinner and the light returns.
rooms.4002: The path gives out at the foot of a lone, steep-sided mountain, and a narrow trail scrambles on through tumbled boulders to the black mouth of a cave in its north face. Cold air breathes out of the opening, smelling of wet stone. Grey hills crowd around in a threatening ring, their grassy flanks broken by outcrops of rock. East, the land climbs into the mountains proper, while the path winds back south down among the hills.
rooms.6602: Dark spruce and larch draw back here from a small clearing at the edge of the taiga, where the ground begins to climb toward the mountains looming to the north. A ring of blackened stones marks an old campfire, and a few logs have been dragged around it for seats, their bark rubbed smooth. Snow lies in crusted drifts beneath the trees, trampled flat around the fire. The forest runs on east and south, a sea of dark needles under a low grey sky.
rooms.6610: A shelf of grey rock juts from the mountainside here, barely wide enough for two to stand abreast, with a dizzy drop beneath and the wind tearing at your cloak. In the cliff to the north a stout wooden door is set into a doorway cut from the living stone. Carved faces flank it on either side, worn almost featureless by centuries of ice and wind. A narrow, crumbling way leads down the rock toward the lower slopes.
rooms.6612: The taiga thins out here at its northern edge, the spruce shrinking to stunted, wind-bent trees no taller than a man. Beyond them the open tundra begins, a grey-brown waste of moss and frozen tussocks stretching away north and east under a hard white sky. A thin rime of frost covers the ground, printed with several sets of boot tracks that all look recent. South and west the dark forest closes in again, its needles hissing in the bitter wind.
rooms.12003: The main warehouse of Port Halyon is built around an open yard, and here two towering walls of salt-stained stone meet in a corner under the grey sky. Bales and barrels stand stacked in roped tiers against the stonework, and the cobbles are slick with spilled oil. A timber stair climbs up the wall to the Guild Office, and worn steps lead down into the basement. A door in the south wall opens on the porters' kitchen, while the yard runs on north and east between more stacks of cargo.
rooms.12005: The canal begins here, its green water let in from the river through a channel lined with dressed stone. A cobbled towpath runs along the quay, and an old iron gate stands in the town wall beside it, rusted fast and laced with creepers that have grown through its bars for years. Through them you glimpse barren, sun-scorched country stretching away toward the desert. The towpath follows the canal east into the town, and a stone stair leads south down to the covered boathouse on the river.
rooms.12006: A long boathouse of tarred timber straddles the river here on stout piles, its roof spanning the water so that boats slide through beneath the rafters as though down a dim hall. The river runs wide and brown between the landing stages, slapping at the piles and filling the shed with the smell of mud and weed. Lanterns hang from the beams, and iron mooring rings are set along the walkways. Upstream the water opens west toward the desert, downstream it runs east toward the sea, and a stair climbs north to the canal quay.
rooms.12007: This cramped back room of the Weapons Shop is a storeroom packed almost to the ceiling with crates of blades and armour, many still stencilled with the marks of foundries along the coast. Racks of spears lean against the walls, and a grindstone on a wooden frame stands in the one clear corner beside a bench stained dark with oil. No window lets in the light, and the air smells of iron, grease and sawdust. The only way out is the door back east into the shop.
rooms.12010: The warehouse basement was dug deep into the riverbank, and in this corner its vaulted roof gave way long ago, leaving a sunken yard open to the sky between walls of mossy stone. Coarse grass has taken the silt floor, worn bare in a broad ring of raked sand where a battered wooden post stands, hacked and splintered by practice blows. The yard runs on north toward the rest of the drill ground, and east the vaults still hold over a darker stretch of the basement. Steps cut into the wall climb up to the main warehouse.
rooms.12015: A broad roof of heavy beams covers this corner of the warehouse, and the shade beneath it is cool and dim after the open yard. Sacks of grain and bolts of sailcloth are piled high on raised pallets to keep them off the damp flagstones, and the low ceiling is hung with hooks and pulley blocks. A narrow wooden stair climbs up to the Supervisor's Office. The covered bay opens east onto more of the warehouse, and south into the yard.
rooms.12018: Great double doors stand open in the warehouse wall here, wide enough for two carts to pass, and a hoisting beam juts out above them with a block and tackle swaying in the wind. The cobbles are grooved by iron-shod wheels and dusted with chaff from cargo hauled up off the river dock to the south. East, a rope rail marks where carters wait their turn at the customs cage, and the sharp tang of vinegar and lye drifts from the first-aid station to the west. Above the doors stands a weathered bronze statue of a porter bowed beneath a sack.
rooms.12019: A broad stone quay runs beside the canal here, its edge lined with iron bollards and fat rope fenders where barges tie up to unload. The great stone bulk of the warehouse rises over the dock, and its wide river doors stand open to the north. Wooden cranes lean out over the green water, and the paving is stained with tar, brine and spilled grain. The canal flows on east toward the sea, and the towpath runs back west along the water.
rooms.12022: This end of the warehouse yard lies open to the sky, and the salt wind gusts across cobbles strewn with straw and broken barrel staves. Timber scaffolding clings to the high wall here, where masons have been patching the stonework after the winter storms, and dried splashes of mortar whiten the ground beneath it. The yard runs on south between stacked cargo, and to the west a roofed bay offers shelter under heavy beams.
rooms.12023: Cargo waits here in the open yard in long rows, barrels of salt fish and lamp oil lashed under tarred canvas against the weather. Chalked marks on the canvas tell which ship brought each load and which merchant claims it. The din of shouted orders and rumbling wheels rolls in from the busy entrance to the south, while the yard stretches on north toward the far corner. The stones underfoot are dark with brine seeping from the barrels.
rooms.12024: A tall archway pierces the warehouse wall here, opening onto North Main Street to the east. Just inside the arch the cobbles widen into a crowded entrance court where wagons are unloaded and their cargo tallied. South, the iron bars of the bonded area wall off goods held for the customs house, and north the open yard runs on between stacked bales. Above the arch a carved anchor and the faded words PORT HALYON WAREHOUSE are cut into the keystone.
rooms.12029: The great North Gate of Port Halyon stands shut and barred, its iron-bound doors set between two squat towers of salt-grey stone. A heavy beam rests across them in iron brackets, and the paving before the gate is caked with dried mud carried in long ago from the road beyond. Arrow slits look out from the towers over the countryside, and an empty brazier stand rusts beside the guard post. Main Street leads back south into the town, where the smell of the bakery hangs on the air.
rooms.12031: North Main Street climbs here between tall merchant houses whose carved balconies lean out over the paving, hung with pots of herbs and lines of washing. The flagstones are polished by countless feet and cartwheels, and the street rings with the cries of hawkers and the creak of signs. It rises north toward Main Street and the North Gate, and falls away south to the crossing where Wharf Avenue meets the road. West, a tall archway opens into the great stone warehouse.
rooms.12035: The South Gate is a pair of tall bronze doors, green with age and salt, closed and locked between towers of weathered stone. Through the grille set in one leaf you can see a worn road leading away from the port into low, scrubby hills. South Main Street runs north from here into the town. A small shop crouches against the wall to the east, and a thin pink mist curls out from under its door with a smell of sulphur and singed hair.
rooms.12036: The dock master's private office is richly furnished with goods brought in from every port on the Sea of Storms: thick carpets, lamps of coloured glass, and a massive carved desk heaped with manifests, harbour dues and tide tables. A great chart of the coast covers one wall, stuck with pins marking every ship expected in port. Potted plants and cut flowers crowd the windowsill and every shelf, filling the room with a green scent. French doors open east onto the waiting room, and a wooden door leads south to the Council Room.
rooms.12039: Wharf Avenue runs wide and straight here, its paving grooved by heavy carts bound for the quays. Ship's chandlers, rope-walks and sailmakers' lofts line the way, their signs creaking in the salt wind, and the smell of tar and fish grows stronger with every step. Above the rooftops the long arches of the old aqueduct stride across the skyline. The avenue carries on east toward the quays and the East Gate, and back west to the crowded crossing with North Main Street.
rooms.12043: Long benches of polished oak line the walls of this tall chamber, where petitioners wait their turn to see the dock master. A clerk's high desk stands by the door with an appointment book chained to it and a brass bell on a bracket above. Portraits of past dock masters, stern men and women in sea coats, gaze down from the panelling. A door to the west leads to the dock master's private office, another opens east into the Office Of The Court Clerk, and a hallway runs south to the foyer.
rooms.12044: The entrance foyer of the Capitol is a lofty hall under a painted dome, where ships in full sail chase one another around a great compass rose. The marble floor rings under every footstep, and benches for messengers stand along the walls beneath tall lamps. A heavy bronze door to the west leads into the Council Room, and a hallway runs north to the waiting room. Broad marble stairs sweep down and out of the building to the street.
rooms.12049: Altoor's Workshop is a cluttered, smoke-stained den behind the Mage's Shop. Workbenches along the walls are crowded with beakers, coiled glass tubes and crucibles, and the air reeks of sulphur, scorched wool and something like burning tar. In the middle of the floor a circle of chalked runes is blackened by fire, and a heap of grey cinders inside it looks uncomfortably as if it was once a person. The only way out is the steel-bound door west into the shop.
rooms.12050: The Office Of The Court Clerk doubles as the harbour court, where quarrels over cargo, wages and dues are settled. The clerk's desk sits below a raised bench, with a railed witness stand beside it and rows of plain benches facing them both. Behind the bench hangs the seal of the harbour council, an anchor wound about with rope. A door to the east leads to the Mayor's Office, the Records Room lies to the south, and the waiting room is back to the west.
rooms.12051: Two tall towers rise from the city wall here, crowned with watch platforms that look out over the harbour and the docks. Between them a heavy timber gate bound with iron closes the archway, opening east onto the covered loading dock by the canal. The paving is crusted with salt and strewn with straw blown in from the quays. Wharf Avenue leads back west into the heart of the port.
rooms.12062: Warm, sweet air fills the bakery of Port Halyon, heavy with the smell of fresh loaves, honey cakes and hard ship's biscuit. A great brick oven glows behind the counter, and long wooden paddles hang on pegs beside its iron door. Flour dusts every surface, from the scrubbed shelves to the beams overhead. The only door leads east onto Main Street.
rooms.12063: This is the busiest general store on the waterfront, and its shelves sag under everything a sailor or traveller might need: coils of rope, lanterns and lamp oil, tinderboxes, oilskin coats and casks of hard biscuit. Nets and buckets hang from hooks in the low ceiling, and a long counter scarred by years of trade runs the length of the room. The smell of tar and soap mixes in the close air. The door opens south onto Wharf Avenue.
rooms.15061: A faint track leaves the King's Road here and wanders south across rolling, scrubby hills, so little used that grass and thistle have almost swallowed it. The paved road lies only a few strides away to the north, yet the noise of its traffic already sounds far off. On either hand stand low cottages of fieldstone, empty and silent, their doors hanging open to the east and west. The wind moves through the long grass with a dry whisper.
rooms.15062: The overgrown track dips into a fold between grassy hills, where broom and bramble crowd so close that you must push them aside. To the east the ground climbs to a bare crest with wide views over the plains, and to the west a deserted cottage sits half hidden in nettles. The track runs back north toward the King's Road and drops south toward the town gates. A scarecrow in faded rags leans over a forgotten garden plot.
rooms.15065: The rutted dirt track crosses open grassland here between two abandoned houses, their shutters nailed tight and their thatch black with rot. The house to the north still has its roof, but the one to the east stands dark and silent, and even the wind seems to hush beside it. A sour smell of decay drifts up from the south, where the track continues. West, the tall grass rolls away toward the empty plains.
rooms.15067: The dirt road ends at the edge of a great pit, and here the smell of decay becomes almost unbearable. The pit is a mass grave, its sides crumbling into a jumble of bones, skulls and rotting shrouds, and some of the bodies look far too fresh for a village that has stood empty for years. Rank grass grows tall and dark around its rim. A narrow track leads back north to the road, an empty house stands to the west, and open plains stretch away east and south.
rooms.15068: The road runs here right through the gutted shell of a house that once straddled it, in at one gaping doorway and out at the other, under the charred beams of what is left of the roof. Furniture lies smashed and flung against the walls as if a whirlwind had raged through, yet strangely no dust or cobweb lies on any of it. A side door opens east onto the grassland and another west into a neighbouring ruin. The road leads on north into the hills, and south to the twin towers of the Northern Gatehouse.
rooms.15071: Beside the road stands the burned-out shell of a small shop, its roof gone and its walls charred black, two of them burnt down to half their height. Through the gaps you can see the scorched stump of a counter and heaps of ash where goods once stood. Weeds and wildflowers have begun to creep in over the blackened sill. The road runs on east across the plains and back west toward the city gate, while open grassland falls away south.

6610.description: The faces were once bearded and stern, perhaps dwarves or kings, but frost has eaten away their features until only the hollows of eyes and mouths remain. Someone has rubbed soot into one pair of eyes, so that it seems to watch you.

12018.description: The porter is cast mid-stride, his back bent under a great sack and his face set in grim patience. Letters on the plinth read: THIS PORT WAS CARRIED HERE ON BACKS LIKE MINE.

12036.description: The chart shows the coast from the river mouth to the open sea, the safe channels inked in blue and the reefs in red. One pin marks a ship many days overdue, and beside it someone has written a single word: STORM.

12050.description: The seal is carved in dark oak and gilded: an anchor with a rope wound about its shank, ringed by the words BY TIDE AND TALLY. The gilt is worn away where nervous hands have touched it for luck.
